csrs.name: fflags
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Unprivileged ISA (20240411), 'F' extension, section 'Floating-Point Control and Status Register': fflags is CSR 0x001, a 5-bit read/write register (NV bit 4, DZ bit 3, OF bit 2, UF bit 1, NX bit 0). The F/D control state is a single 8-bit CSR fcsr = {frm[7:5], fflags[4:0]}, of which this register is the low field's view; a write here writes only bits 4:0 of the same state, and the accumulator semantics are exercised by CASE=fp.precise_flags_and_boxing rather than by a write/read-back rule because a flag is raised by an FP operation, not by a software write.

csrs.name: frm
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Unprivileged ISA (20240411), 'F' extension, section 'Floating-Point Control and Status Register': frm is CSR 0x002, the 3-bit rounding-mode field fcsr[7:5]; encodings 000 RNE, 001 RTZ, 010 RDN, 011 RUP, 100 RMM, 111 dynamic (the instruction's rm field), 101/110 reserved. It is the high field's view of the same fcsr state; the reserved encodings are stored as written and the FP unit resolves a reserved mode as RNE, which is the behaviour fp.operation_matrix already pins for the instruction's rm field.

csrs.name: fcsr
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Unprivileged ISA (20240411), 'F' extension, section 'Floating-Point Control and Status Register': fcsr is CSR 0x003, an 8-bit read/write register holding frm in bits 7:5 and fflags in bits 4:0; fflags (0x001) and frm (0x002) are the constituent views of the same state. The architectural accumulation of fflags is exercised by CASE=fp.precise_flags_and_boxing, where a retiring floating-point operation merges its flags and a squashed one contributes nothing; this table entry makes fcsr a real, generated, privilege-checked register rather than a hardcoded address.

csrs.name: mstatus
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L303 '0x300 & MRW & mstatus'. src/machine.tex: section 'Machine Status Registers (mstatus and mstatush)' L363, 'The mstatus register is an MXLEN-bit read/write register' L365; RV64 layout figure mstatusreg L441-L520, bit-number header rows L448-L495 and field-name rows L462-L474 / L497-L511 (SD 63, WPRI 62:38, MBE 37, SBE 36, SXL 35:34, UXL 33:32, WPRI 31:23, TSR 22, TW 21, TVM 20, MXR 19, SUM 18, MPRV 17, XS 16:15, FS 14:13, MPP 12:11, VS 10:9, SPP 8, MPIE 7, UBE 6, SPIE 5, WPRI 4, MIE 3, WPRI 2, SIE 1, WPRI 0); mstatush is 'For RV32 only' L522 and is therefore excluded. Per-field rules: xPP WARL and 'If privilege mode x is not implemented, then x/PP must be read-only 0' L621-L623; SXL read-only zero without S-mode L646-L647; UXL read-only zero without U-mode L651-L652; 'MPRV is read-only 0 if U-mode is not supported' L688; MXR read-only 0 without S-mode L697-L698; SUM read-only 0 without S-mode L718-L719; MBE/SBE/UBE WARL L727-L728, SBE read-only 0 without S-mode L736, UBE read-only 0 without U-mode L740, 'An implementation supports only little-endian memory accesses if fields MBE, SBE, and UBE are all read-only 0' L767-L768; TVM read-only 0 without S-mode L821; TW read-only 0 with no mode less privileged than M L841-L842; TSR read-only 0 without S-mode L860-L861; FS read-only zero without F or S-mode L928; VS read-only zero without V or S-mode L944; 'XS field is read-only zero' L950. Reset: section 'Reset' L2839, 'The mstatus fields MIE and MPRV are reset to 0' L2842-L2843, 'If little-endian memory accesses are supported, the mstatus/mstatush field MBE is reset to 0' L2844-L2845, 'All other hart state is unspecified' L2858; MosaicRV sets MPP=0b11 so no WARL field holds an illegal value (L2857), giving reset = 3<<11 = 0x1800. p0 is M-mode only and little-endian (config/profiles/p0.json), which forces every field except MPIE/SPIE/MIE/SIE to read-only zero and MPP to read-only 0b11.; FS [14:13] and VS [10:9] are WARL extension-state fields. When the F extension is implemented FS shall not be read-only zero and reads as Dirty when any floating-point state is dirty; the same holds for VS and the V extension. A profile claiming neither reads them as zero Field-level rules the RTL implements and the generator narrows per profile: MPP (12:11) holds the previous privilege (only M in an M-only profile, 'implementations that support only M-mode may hardwire MPP to 3'); SPP (8) the same for a trap into S; MPRV (17) 'is read-only 0 if U-mode is not supported' and otherwise selects MPP as the effective privilege of loads and stores; SUM (18) and MXR (19) adjust S-mode page permissions and are read-only 0 with no S-mode; TVM (20), TW (21) and TSR (22) intercept S-mode satp access, WFI and SRET respectively and are read-only 0 with no S-mode. tools/gen_manifest.py subtracts exactly those bits for a profile whose privilege_modes list has no S or U, so one table describes every profile.

csrs.name: misa
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L304 '0x301 & MRW & misa'. src/machine.tex: section 'Machine ISA Register (misa)' L19, 'The misa CSR is a WARL read-write register reporting the ISA supported by the hart' L22; Fig. misareg L29-L47 (MXL[1:0] = bits MXLEN-1:MXLEN-2 WARL, bits MXLEN-3:26 = '0 (WARL)', Extensions[25:0] WARL); 'The MXL field may be writable in implementations that support multiple base ISAs' L51-L52 and 'The MXL field is always set to the widest supported ISA variant at reset' L54-L55; Table misabase L58-L71 (MXL 1=32, 2=64, 3=128); 'The Extensions field is a WARL field that can contain writable bits where the implementation allows the supported ISA to be modified. At reset, the Extensions field shall contain the maximal set of supported extensions' L96-L99; Table misaletters 'All bits that are reserved for future use must return zero when read' L147-L149; section 'Reset' L2846-L2847 'The misa register is reset to enable the maximal set of supported extensions and widest MXLEN'. p0 implements RV64IM only, so MXL reads 2 and only extension bits I(8) and M(12) are set; writable bits are optional in the spec, so the whole register is modelled read-only. Reset = (2<<62)|(1<<8)|(1<<12) = 0x8000000000001100 = 9223372036854780160.

csrs.name: medeleg
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Machine Trap Delegation Registers (medeleg and mideleg)' L1237; Fig. medelegreg L1310-L1324 (the entire MXLEN field is labelled 'Synchronous Exceptions (WARL)'); 'medeleg has a bit position allocated for every synchronous exception ... with the index of the bit position equal to the value returned in the mcause register' L1326-L1329; 'For exceptions that cannot occur in less privileged modes, the corresponding medeleg bits should be read-only zero. In particular, medeleg[11] is read-only zero' L1354-L1356. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L305 '0x302 & MRW & medeleg'. p0 is M-only (config/profiles/p0.json privilege_modes ['M']), so no synchronous exception can occur in a less privileged mode and every bit is WARL whose only legal value is 0. The register exists at 0x302 and accepts writes, but each written bit canonicalises to 0, so a read always returns 0. Implementation choice, permitted by 'An implementation shall not have any bits of medeleg be read-only one': only the exceptions this profile can actually raise in S or U mode are delegatable -- bits 9:0, the instruction/load/store misaligned and access faults, the breakpoint, the illegal instruction and the two lower-mode environment calls. Bit 11 (ECALL from M-mode) is read-only zero, because an exception taken in M-mode is never delegated ('Traps never transition from a more-privileged mode to a less-privileged mode'), and the page-fault bits 12/13/15 are delegatable exactly when the profile also implements address translation: tools/gen_manifest.py derives them from whether the profile's own CSR table owns satp (I-045 landed the walker), so a profile without translation keeps them read-only zero without a hand edit, and p0 keeps every bit read-only zero because it has no S or U mode for a delegation target to be.

csrs.name: mideleg
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Machine Trap Delegation Registers (medeleg and mideleg)' L1237; Fig. midelegreg L1333-L1347 (the entire MXLEN field is labelled 'Interrupts (WARL)'); 'mideleg holds trap delegation bits for individual interrupts, with the layout of bits matching those in the mip register' L1349-L1352; Sec 'Machine Interrupt Registers (mip and mie)' L1412-L1414 'if register mideleg exists, bit i is not set in mideleg'. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L306 '0x303 & MRW & mideleg'. With no S or U mode there is no delegation target, so every bit is WARL whose only legal value is 0; writes are accepted and each bit canonicalises to 0, and a read always returns 0. Implementation choice, allowed by 'Version 1.11 and earlier prohibited having any bits of mideleg corresponding to machine-level interrupts (but may do so for lower-level interrupts)': bits 3, 7 and 11 (MSI/MTI/MEI) are WARL whose only legal value is 0, because a machine-level interrupt is not taken in a less-privileged mode. Bit 9 (SEI) is read-only zero because the platform has no supervisor external source. Bit 5 (STI) and bit 1 (SSI) are delegatable in a profile with S-mode: the platform timer raises STIP, so the supervisor timer interrupt is a real source, and the software-written SSIP is the other. In a profile with no S or U mode every bit is read-only zero, which is the rule the generator applies.

csrs.name: mie
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Machine Interrupt Registers (mip and mie)' L1358, 'the mie register is the corresponding MXLEN-bit read/write register containing interrupt enable bits' L1361-L1363; 'Interrupt cause number i ... corresponds with bit i in both mip and mie. Bits 15:0 are allocated to standard interrupt causes only, while bits 16 and above are designated for platform or custom use' L1364-L1367; Fig. miereg L1387-L1401; Fig. miereg-standard L1482-L1522 with bits 11/7/3 named MEIE/MTIE/MSIE (L1502, L1506, L1510) and the remaining standard bits drawn as literal '0'; 'A bit in mie must be writable if the corresponding interrupt can ever become pending. Bits of mie that are not writable must be read-only zero' L1432-L1434. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L307 '0x304 & MRW & mie'. p0 has a CLINT (config/memory/p0.json) driving MTIP and MSIP and no PLIC, so MTIE(7) and MSIE(3) are writable and every other bit is write-preserve-zero. Bit 1 (SSIE) is the enable for the software-written SSIP, and bit 5 (STIE) is the enable for the supervisor timer interrupt the platform raises (STIP). Both exist in a profile with S-mode and are read-only zero without one, which is the rule the generator applies. Bit 9 (SEIE) has no source and is read-only zero. Bits 3 and 7 (MSIE, MTIE) are the machine software and timer enables.

csrs.name: mtvec
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Machine Trap-Vector Base-Address Register (mtvec)' L1154, 'The mtvec register is an MXLEN-bit WARL read/write register' L1156-L1157; Fig. mtvecreg L1160-L1176 (BASE[MXLEN-1:2] WARL at bits 63:2, MODE[1:0] WARL at bits 1:0); 'The mtvec register must always be implemented, but can contain a read-only value' L1179-L1180; 'The value in the BASE field must always be aligned on a 4-byte boundary' L1181-L1183; Table mtvec MODE L1192-L1204 (0 = Direct, 1 = Vectored, >=2 = Reserved). Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L308 '0x305 & MRW & mtvec'. MosaicRV accepts MODE 0 and MODE 1; MODE >= 2 is Reserved and canonicalises to 0, and BASE[1:0] is always forced to 0. No reset value is specified by the spec; 0 (Direct mode, base 0) is the conservative choice and is a legal WARL value per L2857 'No WARL field contains an illegal value'.

csrs.name: mcounteren
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Machine Counter-Enable Register (mcounteren)' L1741, 'The counter-enable register mcounteren is a 32-bit register' L1744-L1746; Fig. mcounteren L1748-L1781 (CY 0, TM 1, IR 2, HPM3..HPM31 bits 3..31); 'The settings in this register only control accessibility' L1784-L1786; 'In systems with U-mode, the mcounteren must be implemented, but all fields are WARL and may be read-only zero' L1820-L1823 and 'In systems without U-mode, the mcounteren register should not exist' L1824. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L309 '0x306 & MRW & mcounteren'. p0 is M-only (no U-mode), so every counter is always accessible from the only implemented mode and mcounteren gates nothing there; the register is still modelled with a defined reset of 0 (L2857 makes 0 a legal WARL value) rather than trapping on a read. Recorded deviation: the spec says the register 'should not exist' in a system without U-mode; MosaicRV keeps it at 0x306 as an all-zero WARL register so firmware reads a defined value instead of taking an illegal-instruction trap, and 0 is a legal WARL value (L2857). CY/TM/IR (bits 2:0) gate U-mode reads of cycle/time/instret ('When the CY, TM, IR ... bit in mcounteren is clear, attempts to read ... while executing in U-mode will cause an illegal instruction exception'), and HPM3-HPM31 (bits 3:31) gate the hpmcounter3..31 shadows. All 32 bits are writable, which is the platform declaration this project is verified against: the ACT4 sail.json for the profile sets mcounteren_writable_bits = 0xFFFF_FFFF, so firmware that enables counters (rvtest_setup.h 'csrw mcounteren, t0' with t0 = -1) must observe the bits set or an S-mode read of a counter shadow traps where the reference reads zero. Bits 31:3 were previously read-only zero, which made the RTL's mcounteren disagree with the platform declaration. tools/gen_manifest.py narrows CY/TM/IR back to read-only zero for a profile with no U-mode, where there is no access to gate.

csrs.name: mscratch
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Machine Scratch Register (mscratch)' L1891, 'The mscratch register is an MXLEN-bit read/write register dedicated for use by machine mode' L1893-L1894; Fig. mscratchreg L1898-L1912 (no field decomposition, the whole MXLEN bits are the register). Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L314 '0x340 & MRW & mscratch'. The spec imposes no field constraints, so every 64-bit value is legal and reads back unchanged; 'warl' is the honest encoding because csr.schema.json has no plain read/write behavior token and this register is exactly an unconstrained WARL field. The spec does not specify a reset value; 0 is used.

csrs.name: mepc
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Machine Exception Program Counter (mepc)' L1932, 'The low bit of mepc (mepc[0]) is always zero. On implementations that support only IALIGN=32, the two low bits (mepc[1:0]) are always zero' L1935-L1937; 'mepc is a WARL register that must be able to hold all valid virtual addresses' L1945-L1950; 'When a trap is taken into M-mode, mepc is written with the virtual address of the instruction that was interrupted or that encountered the exception' L1959-L1962; Fig. mepcreg L1964-L1978. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L315 '0x341 & MRW & mepc'. IALIGN is a property of the profile, not of this register, so the table declares the low two bits with `ialign_bits` and tools/gen_manifest.py derives their writability from whether the profile claims the C extension: for a profile that does not, mepc[1:0] are read-only zero, and for one that does, only mepc[0] is. Reset is not specified by the spec; 0 is used and is a legal WARL value.

csrs.name: mcause
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Machine Cause Register (mcause)' L1981, 'The mcause register is an MXLEN-bit read-write register' L1984-L1985, 'The Interrupt bit in the mcause register is set if the trap was caused by an interrupt. The Exception Code field contains a code identifying the last exception or interrupt ... The Exception Code is a WLRL field, so is only guaranteed to hold supported exception codes' L1990-L1995; Fig. mcausereg L1998-L2014 (Interrupt = bit MXLEN-1 = 63, Exception Code = bits MXLEN-2:0 = 62:0); Table mcauses L2017-L2065. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L316 '0x342 & MRW & mcause'. Reset: Sec 'Reset' L2850-L2852 'The mcause register is set to a value indicating the cause of the reset' and L2860-L2862 'the value 0 should be returned on implementations that do not distinguish different reset conditions'; p0 does not distinguish reset causes, so reset is 0.

csrs.name: mtval
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Machine Trap Value Register (mtval)' L2169, 'The mtval register is an MXLEN-bit read-write register' L2171-L2172; 'The hardware platform will specify which exceptions must set mtval informatively and which may unconditionally set it to zero. If the hardware platform specifies that no exceptions set mtval to a nonzero value, then mtval is read-only zero' L2175-L2179; 'If mtval is not read-only zero, it is a WARL register that must be able to hold all valid virtual addresses and the value zero' L2259-L2267; Fig. mtvalreg L2196-L2207. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L317 '0x343 & MRW & mtval'. MosaicRV declares mtval not read-only zero and therefore implements it as a full-width WARL register; reset 0 is unspecified by the spec and legal. Which p0 exceptions set mtval informatively is a platform policy outside this table and is recorded as an open ambiguity in results/reports/I-001-csr-m.md.

csrs.name: mip
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Machine Interrupt Registers (mip and mie)' L1358, 'The mip register is an MXLEN-bit read/write register containing information on pending interrupts' L1360-L1361; 'Interrupt cause number i ... corresponds with bit i in both mip and mie. Bits 15:0 are allocated to standard interrupt causes only, while bits 16 and above are designated for platform or custom use' L1364-L1367; Fig. mipreg L1370-L1384; trap conditions (a) MIE, (b) bit i set in both mip and mie, (c) bit i clear in mideleg L1404-L1416; 'Each individual bit in register mip may be writable or may be read-only' L1424-L1430; Fig. mipreg-standard L1440-L1480 with bits 11/7/3 named MEIP/MTIP/MSIP (L1460, L1464, L1468) and all other standard bits drawn as literal '0'. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L318 '0x344 & MRW & mip'. p0 has a CLINT (config/memory/p0.json) driving MTIP and MSIP and no PLIC, so MTIP(7) and MSIP(3) are the implemented bits and every other bit, including MEIP(11), is write-preserve-zero. Bit 1 (SSIP) is writable for the same reason mip.MSIP/MTIP are: a software-writable pending bit must behave like a real one ('a pending interrupt i can be cleared by writing 0 to this bit'). Bit 9 (SEIP) is read-only zero here -- the platform has no supervisor external source. Bit 5 (STIP) is implemented in a profile with S-mode: the platform timer sets it and software may clear it by writing mip[5]=0, and sip exposes the same bit as its own read-only view; a profile without S-mode keeps it read-only zero, which is the rule the generator applies.

csrs.name: mvendorid
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Machine Vendor ID Register (mvendorid)' L190, 'The mvendorid CSR is a 32-bit read-only register providing the JEDEC manufacturer ID of the provider of the core. This register must be readable in any implementation, but a value of 0 can be returned to indicate the field is not implemented or that this is a non-commercial implementation' L192-L196; Fig. mvendorreg L198-L214 (Bank 31:7, Offset 6:0). Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L295 '0xF11 & MRO & mvendorid'. MosaicRV is not a JEDEC-registered commercial vendor, so it returns 0, which the spec explicitly permits.

csrs.name: marchid
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Machine Architecture ID Register (marchid)' L240, 'The marchid CSR is an MXLEN-bit read-only register encoding the base microarchitecture of the hart. This register must be readable in any implementation, but a value of 0 can be returned to indicate the field is not implemented' L242-L245; Fig. marchreg L249-L263 (whole MXLEN bits are Architecture ID); 'Open-source project architecture IDs are allocated globally by RISC-V International, and have non-zero architecture IDs with a zero most-significant-bit (MSB)' L266-L270. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L296 '0xF12 & MRO & marchid'. MosaicRV has not been allocated an architecture ID, so it returns the spec-permitted 0; a non-zero ID must be added before any claim of conformance is made.

csrs.name: mimpid
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Machine Implementation ID Register (mimpid)' L293, 'The mimpid CSR provides a unique encoding of the version of the processor implementation. This register must be readable in any implementation, but a value of 0 can be returned to indicate that the field is not implemented' L295-L298; Fig. mimpidreg L301-L315. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L297 '0xF13 & MRO & mimpid'. No version identifier has been assigned to MosaicRV, so it returns the spec-permitted 0.

csrs.name: mhartid
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Hart ID Register (mhartid)' L327, 'The mhartid CSR is an MXLEN-bit read-only register containing the integer ID of the hardware thread running the code. This register must be readable in any implementation ... but at least one hart must have a hart ID of zero. Hart IDs must be unique within the execution environment' L329-L334; Fig. mhartidreg L336-L350. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L298 '0xF14 & MRO & mhartid'. config/profiles/p0.json sets harts = 1, so the only MosaicRV hart is hart 0 and mhartid returns 0, satisfying the 'at least one hart must have a hart ID of zero' rule.

csrs.name: mcycle
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Hardware Performance Monitor' L1648, 'The mcycle CSR counts the number of clock cycles executed by the processor core on which the hart is running ... The mcycle and minstret registers have 64-bit precision on all RV32 and RV64 systems' L1650-L1655; 'The counter registers have an arbitrary value after the hart is reset, and can be written with a given value. Any CSR write takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed' L1657-L1659; Fig. hardware performance monitor counters L1673-L1692. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L363 '0xB00 & MRW & mcycle'. Recorded deviation from the task card: the spec table marks mcycle MRW and the text says it 'can be written with a given value', so access is 'rw' and behavior is 'warl' (every 64-bit value is legal and reads back); 'fixed' with access 'ro' would falsely claim the counter is immutable. The post-reset value is arbitrary per L1657, so 0 is the conservative deterministic choice.

csrs.name: minstret
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Hardware Performance Monitor' L1648, 'The minstret CSR counts the number of instructions the hart has retired. The mcycle and minstret registers have 64-bit precision on all RV32 and RV64 systems' L1653-L1655; 'The counter registers have an arbitrary value after the hart is reset, and can be written with a given value' L1657-L1659. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L364 '0xB02 & MRW & minstret'. Same recorded deviation as mcycle: architecturally MRW and writable, so 'rw'/'warl' rather than 'ro'/'fixed'; post-reset value arbitrary per L1657, so 0 is used.

csrs.name: cycle
csrs.spec_clause: RISC-V Privileged Spec v1.12, tag Priv-v1.12 commit 98964261c931d51884f733664b22efe43de93033, src/machine.tex: section 'Machine Counter-Enable Register (mcounteren)' L1805-L1810, 'The cycle, instret, and hpmcounter_n CSRs are read-only shadows of mcycle, minstret, and mhpmcounter_n, respectively ... Analogously, on RV32I the cycleh, instreth and hpmcounter_nh CSRs are read-only shadows of mcycleh, minstreth and mhpmcounter_nh' (so cycleh is an RV32-only alias); section 'Hardware Performance Monitor' L1653-L1655 gives mcycle 64-bit precision on RV64, so cycle is 64 bits wide here. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L166 '0xC00 & URO & cycle'. M-mode code may access all lower-privilege CSRs, so cycle is readable from M. Reset 0 because mcycle resets to 0.

csrs.name: time

Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L170-L199 assign '0xC03 & URO & hpmcounter3' through '0xC1F & URO & hpmcounter31'. src/machine.tex section 'Hardware Performance Monitor' L1653-L1655: hpmcounter26 is the read-only shadow of mhpmcounter26, and a counter that is not implemented reads as zero, so an implementation with no HPM counter must answer a read at 0xc1a with 0 rather than trap. The capability ladder advertises Zihpm from p0 with that clause, so a profile with no U-mode (p0) must still implement the shadow: this row is in the M block, and a profile with U-mode (p1..p3) declares the same register in csr/mode_su.json; tools/gen_manifest.py merges the two declarations and refuses them if they disagree. No mhpmcounter26, mhpmevent26 or mcountinhibit is implemented (config/csr/mode_m.json declares none), so the shadow is read-only zero; reset 0 is the only value it can hold.
